Eligible IC+ commercial card transactions can qualify for network savings, customer reconciliation is a separate benefit, and Klarna/PayPal can use line items in underwriting with only potential approval improvements. The card program covers US domestic excluding territories and intra-EU transactions, with Visa/Mastercard/AmEx scope, direct AmEx agreement for savings, 200 line items and AmEx transmission of four. Klarna and PayPal merchant country support is separate from global payment method or customer location descriptions (old 6-27, new 7-28).

Payment Intent API data can be supplied during confirmation or at a later supported capture if missing, with ordinary persistence from confirmation to separate capture. PayPal does not support setting line items at capture. For an updated capture, reconcile updated data to the capture amount. Line items require expansion for response display (old 209-211, 324-407 and 466-507, new 202-204, 290-343 and 375-413). Confirmation samples containing a return_url do not prove payment completion. The example create responses can remain requires_payment_method (old 194-203 and 272-321, new 186-196 and 237-287).

Both capture dates distinguish API validation, arithmetic processing and network qualification. A default mismatch returns 400. A request-level opt-out lets the API request proceed with amount_details.error while Stripe withholds mismatched card line data from networks, so those transactions cannot qualify for interchange savings. MCC and tax ineligibility similarly need not create an API rejection (old 37, 706-714, new 40, 612-620). Top-level versus per-line tax and discount are mutually exclusive within each pair (old 124-126, new 126-128). Checkout's tax and order reference auto-populate for L2, while L3 has its own Checkout line-item price/product/quantity field route (old 67-76, new 70-78).

Card/PayPal/Klarna fields can coexist if supported, even when the method is not used to confirm. Klarna's formula belongs to its line data and does not erase the PaymentIntent amount. PayPal sold_by is the selling connected Stripe account ID and is left blank outside that role. Card/PayPal do not send line items alongside travel industry metadata, whereas Klarna's Extra Merchant Data path is private preview (old 26, 128-157, 503-507, new 27, 130-159, 409-413).

findings: Both captures cover amount_details on a manually captured PaymentIntent. Request if_available where the example calls for multicapture, overcapture, incremental authorization or partial authorization. Payment-method support governs availability, and amount_details.line_items requires expansion to appear in the response. The multi-capture section explicitly excludes Klarna and PayPal (old 14-21, 413-417, 660-666, 912-918, new 15-22, 338-344, 531-537, 724-730).

At first capture, add amount_details and/or its line items if absent or include or explicitly unset either when supplied at creation. The general subsequent-capture prose says to keep individually retained fields and cannot introduce fields absent in prior captures. Amounts for discount, tax and shipping sum and line items aggregate. Postal codes may be omitted but cannot change if supplied. An incomplete nonfinal capture remains requires_capture; an explicit final capture or default final capture can transition to succeeded. The special partial-capture finish example passes zero and final_capture=true after the earlier capture, omits amount_details and line_items from the final request, and retains first-capture line items in its response (old 136-142, 231-239, 282-286, 346-362, new 107-113, 182-190, 213-217, 277-289).

Overcapture increases the capture up to maximum_amount_capturable, with amount_details matching the actual capture. Incremental authorization calls increment_authorization up to the payment-method limit, with amount_details matching the new total authorized amount, and the example remains requires_capture with zero amount received (old 540-544, 789-793 and 851-905, new 437-441, 630-634 and 663-717).

Partial authorization can produce amount_details_amount_mismatch when the old items no longer match the smaller approved total. The merchant can reconcile amount_details at capture, clearing the error and allowing Stripe to send card line data to the networks. The unreconciled case can still succeed at capture, but Stripe withholds mismatched card data and the transaction loses eligibility for L2/L3 savings. Network transmission is one prerequisite, not an assertion of actual savings (old 964-1016, 1042-1089, 1104-1147, new 756-808, 821-868, 876-919).

findings: May 6, 2026 and November 7, 2026 both describe Pix as Brazil's bank-to-bank real-time method: Brazilian buyer, BRL presentment, account-country settlement currency, customer review and approval in the banking app using a QR code or Pix string. The November overview distinguishes immediate confirmation timing and settlement up to T+2 from authorization duration, which depends on the buyer. Checkout remains open, the bank app does not redirect back, and Checkout/Elements handles the configured return_url at a terminal intent state. Check that state for actual success (old raw lines 4–33, 55–106, 107–120, 168–180; new raw lines 5–21, 53–75, 228–250).

Pix Automático applies to eligible businesses outside Brazil. The customer authorizes amount and billing cycle in their banking app. SetupIntent establishes a mandate without collecting an initial payment; PaymentIntent makes an initial charge and establishes a mandate. For subsequent payments the bank pre-debit notice precedes charging by three days, the Intent is processing in this interval, and confirmation can take up to seven days with retries. Over-limit recurring payments fail. When a Charge exists its payment_method_details.pix.mandate identifies the Mandate. Merchant detachment revokes it and prevents reuse; bank-app customer revocation sends mandate.updated, then a new on-session mandate is needed (old raw lines 8–10, 94–105 and 182–186; new raw lines 79–83, 146–164 and 185–200).

The November overview makes refund, dispute and capabilities boundaries explicit. Full and partial refunds within 90 days return to the original bank account and cannot be canceled. Usually a few minutes has no guaranteed maximum; Refund object status, request acceptance and actual customer bank credit are distinct. Under MED the customer supplies evidence to their bank, Stripe notifies the merchant via email/Dashboard/charge.dispute.created, and the partner decision cannot be contested or appealed through Stripe. Debit to the Stripe account follows notified partner acceptance. Full disputes are supported; partial disputes and manual/partial/multi/over-capture are marked unsupported (old raw lines 42–52 and 140–146; new raw lines 91–144).

The November eligibility/capability and product matrices include provisional merchant/platform/marketplace access, B2B/B2C, 12 displayed prohibited MCCs, expanded support labels and explicit unsupported entries such as Terminal or Express Checkout Element. For front-end products enable in settings; manually listed integration goes through acceptance guidance. The new Connect ending reiterates the connected-account supported-country/activation condition for direct charges or on_behalf_of and distinguishes who activates by Dashboard type. Retain May platform-as-MoR route as May evidence (old raw lines 94–105, 123–138 and 148–166, 234–243; new raw lines 14–51, 85–115, 166–200 and 276–282).

findings: Both captures explain an eligible payment method authorization as a hold that reserves funds. The Charge card capture_before field is the specific authorization expiry. Successful manual authorization leaves the Intent requires_capture, emits payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated when the customer completes the manual-capture payment process, and allows inspection of amount_capturable. Capture uses a PaymentIntent ID, including for Checkout, and defaults to the authorized amount. If an entirely uncaptured authorization expires, release and canceled follow, and merchant cancellation uses the PaymentIntent (old 8-12, 166-194, new 9-13, 135-159).

The merchant can initiate manual authorization in Dashboard or by setting Checkout Session payment_intent_data.capture_method or the PaymentIntent’s capture_method. Method-level capture_method on card lets only cards take a hold while other eligible payment methods can still be used with their own behavior. After attaching card details/confirming the PaymentIntent, verify authorization rather than inferring from Checkout creation, method selection or a successful API request (old 62-77, 101-166, new 62-77, 91-135).

Per-method hold windows and initial Affirm/Afterpay down-payment/installment treatment remain method-specific (old 18-60, 172-190, new 19-60, 141-155).

Refunds are asynchronous, full or partial within 180 days, and take up to five minutes to complete as documented. Stripe sends refund.updated or refund.failed for the final result; the Refund becomes succeeded or failed, and failure returns the amount to Stripe balance with an alternative refund left to the merchant. Revolut decides disputes after evidence submission; Stripe notifies by email, Dashboard and charge.dispute.created if webhooks are configured, holds the amount until resolution, and returns it or makes the debit permanent based on the decision (old 122-145; new 122-146). Browser return alone establishes no payment status, capture or payout.

findings: The May 11 and November 7, 2026 full captures describe collecting a reusable card in a basic integration for businesses operating primarily in the US and Canada. The guide says this pattern is non-compliant where saving cards requires authentication, such as India, and routes to authentication-capable saving. Its US/Canada qualifier does not promise a bank will never require auth: both show a sandbox auth-required decline branch. For future/offline use display terms and obtain customer opt-in and a written record, including scope, timing/frequency, amount calculation and a subscription cancellation policy when applicable (old raw lines 8–21 and 214–222; new raw lines 9–22 and 194–202).

The merchant needs a Stripe account. The customer enters card data into Stripe-hosted Elements, with live HTTPS and an HTTP testing allowance, Stripe.js directly from js.stripe.com, and a separate postal code input when split Elements are used. The client creates a PaymentMethod and sends only its ID to the server in the described handoff. Merchant server associates it with a new/existing Customers v1 Customer. Subsequent listing examples separately show customer_account for a customer-configured v2 Account and customer for v1; the attach and payment-create samples in this guide use the v1 Customer route (old raw lines 23–95, 108–169; new raw lines 24–97, 115–157).

The later server example creates and confirms a new PaymentIntent with the stored PaymentMethod and error_on_requires_action true. With required customer action the attempt declines; the guide describes HTTP 402, error/decline-code inspection, and bringing the customer back to enter and attach a new method before another payment attempt. The optional one-call branch for an already-created Customer sets setup_future_usage to on_session, i.e. intended future customer-present reuse, without a guarantee of exemption or permission to charge off-session. Creating or attaching the method is separate from later success (old raw lines 169–222; new raw lines 157–202).

The optional CVC path is a separate customer-present browser confirmation using a server-created PaymentIntent client secret, the selected saved PaymentMethod ID and cardCvc Element. Read succeeded and use a payment_intent.succeeded webhook/plugin for critical post-payment actions because the browser callback can be lost. Failed CVC can coexist with a succeeded payment, so Radar settings matter if the merchant wants to block these. The main recipe is not evidence that all branches need no webhooks (old raw lines 224–260; new raw lines 204–240).

findings: Both captures describe reusable, delayed, business-initiated EUR SEPA Core with personal and business accounts, no SEPA B2B scheme, no manual capture, and EUR 10,000 each plus EUR 10,000 additional weekly cap for new users. Customer-location property EU and same 40 Stripe business-account locations are separate. Both require additional identity verification after requesting payment-method access. November adds the requirement to collect billing city, postal_code, line1 and country for payments from IBANs outside the EEA, in addition to customer name, IBAN and accepted mandate. The Charge carries Mandate ID (old 6–118, new 7–119). This does not convert the EU customer label or IBAN condition into an individual eligibility guarantee. Source 13–23 omits identity verification and dated address requirement.

Both captures retain Dashboard enablement and Checkout, Elements, Payment Links, Subscriptions, Invoicing, Connect and Express Checkout Element exclusion (old 105–149, new 106–149). Merchant must collect customer mandate before debit; customer can cancel via relevant party or bank and further debits under the canceled mandate are invalid. Stripe learns of external cancellation on a failed payment, then sets inactive and emits mandate.updated. Merchant can also cancel via detachment; after cancellation or deactivation obtain a new mandate before later debit (old 216–224,274–288 and new 222–230,280–294).

Timing stays submission-based T+6 at 00:00 UTC for payment success and available Stripe funds, cutoff 10:30 CET, with later submission for non-business and post-cutoff creation, and five-business-day refusal window after submission. `expected_debit_date` on Charge and listed charge events is estimated when determinable, not guaranteed. Most failures occur within six business days of initiation; rare post-window failures can still appear as disputes. Stripe immediately removes balance funds on failure, with Charge failure_code and failure_message (old 152–162,226–272 and new 152–162,232–278). Source 19 omits T's submission basis and failure caution; line 31 labels its 13 listed codes as 12. Concept 73 and provider index 263 repeat the count. The separate May setup guide 20–27 gives a typical five-business-day arrival figure. Preserve the distinction and timing tension without treating either as external-bank payout or an SLA. Checkout depiction 'payment complete' (old/new 130) does not override delayed timeline.

Both captures require notice for each debit, with Stripe default email and always automatic Stripe email when using Stripe Creditor ID. When allowed to customize, Dashboard versus Sources API controls differ; payment_intent.processing is trigger for debit-initiation emails and required details are listed. Standard is at least 14 calendar days before creation, but the mandate must state any shorter timing. The captured Stripe mandate says up to two calendar days before future payments and allows notice at payment creation. Fixed-amount recurring notices can cover multiple dated debits (old/new 164–180). Source 25 and concept 65 phrase two days as the shortest timing, which misses the cited creation-time case.

Connect continues to require platform enablement plus requested connected-account capability. November adds per-connected-account mandate for destination charges on_behalf_of when that account is merchant of record, no cloning SEPA method and mandate to connected accounts for destination charges, and new PaymentIntent or SetupIntent with on_behalf_of to collect customer authorization. Scope the requirement to the documented destination path without generalizing across charge types. findings: Both captures describe a customer authorizing an e-mandate during initial setup in the UPI app with PIN additional factor authentication. An existing mandate allows future automated charges within its terms. Stripe handles the initial charge window of up to five minutes and, with SetupIntent, debits and instantly refunds to avoid requiring AFA for the intended later charge. This does not remove PIN authorization during mandate setup.

Merchant confirms a PaymentIntent for a subsequent recurring payment, which triggers Stripe to send the customer an SMS/app notification with exact debit amount and mandate cancellation option, wait at least 24 hours and then charge. No additional merchant actions are documented after confirmation. Notification and waiting are separate from a successful charge outcome.

With a customer-initiated Adaptive Pricing subscription, automatic e-mandate creation in the selected currency is conditional on mandate support for it. If explicit Checkout Session mandate parameters are provided, they override automatically determined values. The guide tells users seeking the local-currency and exchange-rate handling to omit such parameters.

findings: The merchant can collect a PaymentMethod with Payment Element or directly with a custom frontend. Stripe vaults details and forwarding accepts a PaymentMethod without Customer attachment. For a configured endpoint, the merchant server submits card object ID, exact URL, typed blank placeholders and replacement fields, plus the destination credentials on each API request. Stripe inserts vault card data and sends the outbound request, optionally applying Card Account Updater where enabled/available. It synchronously waits less than one minute for a third-party processor response, redacts identified PCI-sensitive data, stores the redacted response and relays a ForwardingRequest (old 18-28, 42-64, 245-249, 289-293, new 35-54, 68-87, 243-247, 288-292).

Vault and Forward does not confirm or capture PaymentIntents. The separate attempt on Stripe can cause duplicate capture after an external capture, and direct third-party authorization leaves refunds/disputes with that processor. Destination response and actual tokenization/authorization/capture/settlement are separate observations (old 28, 287-293, 756, new 54, 286-292, 734).

Link credentials are excluded and Link card payments should be routed to Stripe. A CVC expires with time or use, can be consumed by SetupIntent-confirmation validation, and may need re-collection if required. Google Pay FPAN uses standard card replacements and Google Pay DPAN uses network token replacements (old 30-40, 103-171, new 56-66, 114-182).

Both captures separate eligible forwarding destinations/countries from where a Stripe account may be registered. Setup needs test account IDs and production destination config. The general endpoint uses HTTPS and JSON/XML request/response and keeps hashed and encrypted versions of destination API keys. Keys shared for endpoint enablement are PGP-protected. The incoming request headers and body are encrypted and appear as encrypted_request in the Dashboard, and restricted forwarding write and optional read permissions serve different operations (old 355-365, 429-433, 558-562, 607-617, 710-720, 758-762, new 338-348, 420-424, 549-553, 598-608, 701-711, 736-740).

findings: May and November say some Stripe Radar model inputs are automatic and others come from the merchant's integration. Payment Links, Checkout, Elements and mobile SDKs collect signals such as device information and IP. Direct integrations typically send client IP/user agent/checkout URL on PaymentIntent and customer email/name/billing address on Customer, and can use Radar Sessions for advanced signals. Elements is recommended with customer factors in the integration table.

Both snapshots give provider estimates of 36% advanced risk factors, 12% IP, 11% email, 3% name and 1% billing address. Integration list order and recommended labels are visible but the right-hand completeness cells are blank in both raws. The capture does not quantify each integration row, establish ranks as measured or establish additive merchant fraud reduction.

Both guides recommend reusing Customer with associated billing address and saved methods for cross-method pattern history, giving email at Customer creation and name when tokenizing, and storing shipping only when physical goods are shipped. They recommend handling declines on manual PaymentIntent creation and tracking repeated attempts if reusing the Intent.

Both advise always loading Stripe.js directly from the provider-hosted script across website pages, not using a local copy, and keeping device/behavior collection in the merchant’s privacy policy. May old raw lines 64–68 prescribe Dahlia in both the snippet and the direct-loading instruction. November new raw lines 65–69 prescribe Endive in both. This is a substantive dated implementation instruction, while Radar's behavior is stable in the captures.

Radar scans on a Charge basis and PaymentIntent retries may yield multiple scanned charges. Saving for future use without a charge is excluded by default. A merchant can opt into SetupIntent scanning in the named Radar setting. The setting does not prove successful setup or charge outcome.
